text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet plans to submit to parliament a draft proposal for setting up of a currency board system based on existing central bank structures, Finance minister Dimitar Kostov said.

-- Bulgaria's main opposition Union of Democratic Forces coalition said it would reform as a political party to press for early parliamentary elections and play its part in leading the country out of the crisis.

-- Bulgaria's National Investigation Service (NIS) will search for evidence of misappropriation by bankers from 13 commercial banks placed in receivership by the central bank, NIS director Boiko Rashkov said.
-- Bulgaria's Interior Ministry said it would set up a special department to fight corruption among police officers.
-- Bulgaria's president elect Petar Stoyanov has asked the European Union to aid Bulgaria with grain and fodder deliveries during the winter.

-- Bulgaria's Energy Minister Roumen Ovcharov is expected to sign an agreement on Wednesday with his Turkish counterpart in Ankara for exports of some 300 million kilowatt hours of electricity to Turkey.
-- Bulgaria's state Motor Insurance Company (MIC) merged into another state insurance company, Bulstrad. The new company will have a capital of 400.4 million levs.
-- Israel-registered Invesco International company is interested in buying 70 percent of Bulgaria's Interpred World Trade Centre in Sofia for $34 million, an Invesco International official said.

-- Bulgaria's domestic debt rose by 27.7 billion levs in October to 668.3 billion levs because of new issues of government securities and a fall in the value of the lev, Finance Ministry figures showed.

-- Bulgarians have withdrawn some 6.5 billion levs deposits from the State Saving Bank (SSB) last week and on Monday out of concerns they might lose their savings if a currency board is introduced in the country, a SSB official said.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet is expected to rise fuel prices with 18 percent from December 1 after a 14-18 percent rise last week, a government official said.
